comments.author: @marcsamuelson1011
comments.text: Canada has a surprisingly restrictive immigration history. Countries like the United States, Brazil, and Argentina began with similarly, maybe a few more or less settlers, but grew much faster. I did not realize how much the English/French rivalry adversely effected immigration. The French would protest if there was too many Anglophone/Protestant immigrants. The English were wary of too many non English speaking/Catholic migrants. That internal conflict seemed to deflate the numbers of immigrants Canada allowed into the country durng the 18th and 19th centuries. The only exception seemed to be the Irish, who spoke English but were also Catholic. Some groups like Ukrainians were brought in to fill up the vast prairies, but even the Germans seemed to be those who did not get land in the United States. Brazil for instance attracted way more German and Japanese immigrants. Italian immigrants settled Brazil and Argentina in droves . Of course, the United States encouraged massive numbers of Southern Italians, but even Australia proportionally attracted more Italian immigrants over the years. Numerically, there are probably about as many Australians of Greek and Italian decent as Canadians, but because Australia is half of Canada's size, the proportion of the population is so much more. It seems like during the last decade Canada is trying to make up for lost time regarding the millions of immigrants. I am cautiously optimistic it will work out for Canada over time.
